ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, this is a schematic diagram of electric energy transmission of a certain power station. It is known that the output voltage of the generator, the resistance of the transmission line, and the numbers of turns of the ideal step-up and step-down transformers all remain unchanged. If the user resistance R0 decreases, which of the following statements is correct?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The voltage obtained by the user decreases

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, this is a schematic diagram of electric energy transmission of a certain power station. It is known that the output voltage of the generator, the resistance of the transmission line, and the numbers of turns of the ideal step-up and step-down transformers all remain unchanged. If the user resistance R0 decreases, how will the voltage obtained by the user change?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The voltage obtained by the user decreases
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is an AC generator, connected to the ideal transformer T1 on the left; the right side of T1 transmits electric energy to the right through two transmission lines, with a resistor R connected in series in the upper transmission line; on the right side is the ideal transformer T2, and the secondary side of T2 is connected to the user resistance R0. Reasoning: The generator output voltage remains unchanged, and the number of turns of the step-up transformer T1 remains unchanged, so the transmission end of T1, that is, the line sending-end voltage, remains unchanged. Convert the user resistance R0 through the ideal step-down transformer T2 on the right side to its primary side; because the turns ratio of T2 remains unchanged, the converted resistance is proportional to R0, so when R0 decreases, the converted resistance also decreases. Thus the total equivalent load seen by the transmission line becomes smaller, and the transmission current increases. The voltage loss on the transmission-line resistance R is IR, and the increase in current makes the line voltage drop increase. The sending-end voltage remains unchanged, while the voltage obtained by the primary side of T2 equals the sending-end voltage minus the line voltage drop, so the primary-side voltage of T2 decreases. The turns ratio of T2 remains unchanged, and the voltage at the secondary-side user terminal changes in a fixed proportion with the primary-side voltage; therefore the voltage obtained by the user decreases.
